title: Run tasks with a concurrency limit
summary: Map over items with an async function, never running more than a fixed number at once, and keep results in input order.
prompt:
Finish `mapLimit(items, limit, fn)`. It calls `fn(item, index)` for every item and resolves with the results **in input order**.

- At most `limit` calls may be in flight at the same time; start the next one as soon as one finishes.
- If any call rejects, the returned promise rejects with that error and no **new** calls are started.
- An empty list resolves to `[]`. Throw a `RangeError` (synchronously or as a rejection) when `limit` is less than 1.
hints: Start `Math.min(limit, items.length)` workers; each loops, taking the next index from a shared counter.
Write results with `results[index] = await fn(...)` so order does not depend on finishing time.
Keep a `failed` flag so workers stop taking new items after an error, and `Promise.all` the workers.
